title: Mind the Trap As LLMs Guess the Data Model: Grain-Aware Guards Against Fan-out in Text-to-SQL and Its Benchmarks
abstract: arXiv:2611.29009v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Text-to-SQL systems built on large language models (LLMs) often aggregate over one-to-many and many-to-many joins, a classic trap: when the joined rows repeat an entity, a SUM or COUNT counts it more than once, yet the query runs and returns a plausible number. We characterize these fan-out errors by one condition on the relation an aggregate reads, which depends on two facts a schema does not show: each measure's grain, and how many rows a join on each key repeats. An audit that tests the condition on the data finds distorted gold answers for 4.2% of the dev questions of BIRD, a widely used benchmark, and BIRD's later, independent revision changed 44% of the answers the audit flags as definite fan-out, against 16% of unflagged ones. We release BIRD-FanOut, 486 BIRD questions with reviewed gold, and GrainTraps, synthetic questions that set this trap and related ones. translated_title: 当LLM猜测数据模型时当心陷阱：面向Text-to-SQL及其基准测试的粒度感知扇出错误防护
translated_abstract: 基于大语言模型（LLM）构建的Text-to-SQL系统经常在一对多和多对多连接上进行聚合，这是一个经典的陷阱：当连接后的行重复同一实体时，SUM或COUNT会对其进行重复计数，但查询仍能正常运行并返回一个看似合理的数字。我们通过聚合所读取关系上的一个条件来刻画这类扇出（fan-out）错误，该条件依赖于模式中并未显示的两个事实：每个度量的粒度，以及每个键上的连接会重复多少行。在数据上检验该条件的审计发现，广泛使用的基准测试BIRD的开发集问题中有4.2%的标准答案被此类错误扭曲；而BIRD后续的独立修订版本更改了审计中标记为确定性扇出错误的答案的44%，相比之下未标记的答案仅有16%被更改。我们发布了BIRD-FanOut数据集（包含486个经过审核标准答案的BIRD问题）以及GrainTraps数据集（专门设置此陷阱及相关陷阱的合成问题）。在八个LLM智能体上的实验表明，从……计算得到的函数依赖（FD）（摘要此处不完整）
tldr: 该论文揭示了LLM驱动的Text-to-SQL系统因一对多连接导致的扇出聚合错误这一经典陷阱，发现广泛使用的BIRD基准中有4.2%的标准答案被此类错误扭曲，并发布了修正后的BIRD-FanOut数据集和GrainTraps合成数据集以帮助防范这类错误。
en_tdlr: This paper exposes the classic fan-out trap in LLM-based Text-to-SQL systems where one-to-many joins distort SUM/COUNT aggregations, shows that 4.2% of BIRD benchmark's gold answers are affected by such errors, and releases the corrected BIRD-FanOut dataset along with GrainTraps synthetic benchmarks to guard against these grain-related errors.
